raw_text:
Here’s a 12‑week, phased plan starting 2026-06-01, designed for a recreational lifter with PCOS to improve body composition and insulin sensitivity while protecting HPA axis function. It prioritizes progressive resistance training, moderate cardio, adequate recovery, and supportive fueling (no crash dieting). Full gym assumed.

Overview
- Training days: 4 resistance days/week + 2 optional low-intensity cardio/mobility days.
- Emphasis: Compound lifts, progressive overload, moderate volume, consistent protein and fiber, circadian-friendly habits.
- Conditioning: Low-to-moderate intensity only; avoid long, exhaustive sessions.
- RPE use: Target ranges provided to autoregulate by readiness.
- Deloads: Built in to manage stress and irregular cycles.
- Measurements: Track waist, hip, weight, a few strength markers, and CGM/fasting glucose if available. Reassess at weeks 4, 8, 12.

Phase structure
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and insulin-sensitizing strength. Build movement quality, moderate volume, consistent protein/carb timing.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Progressive hypertrophy with strength anchors; small increase in volume and intensity.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–11): Intensification and metabolic density; slightly higher density, similar total volume; maintain recovery.
- Week 12: Deload, testing, and transition plan.

Weekly schedule template
- Mon: Lower A (Strength emphasis)
- Tue: Upper A (Strength/hypertrophy mix)
- Wed: Optional LISS 25–35 min + mobility 15 min
- Thu: Lower B (Hypertrophy emphasis)
- Fri: Upper B (Hypertrophy emphasis)
- Sat: Optional LISS 25–35 min or incline walk outside + mobility 15 min
- Sun: Full rest

Intensity guidelines
- Strength sets: RPE 7–8 (2–3 reps in reserve), never to failure.
- Hypertrophy sets: RPE 8–9 (1–2 RIR), last set sometimes 0–1 RIR on isolation only.
- Deload: RPE 6, reduce sets by ~40–50%.

Warm-up (every session, ~10–12 min)
- 5 min easy cardio (bike/row) nasal breathing.
- Dynamic: ankle rocks, 90/90 hips, T-spine openers, band pull-aparts.
- Movement prep: 1–2 ramp-up sets per main lift.

Cool-down (5–8 min)
- Easy walk/bike, parasympathetic breathing (4s inhale, 6–8s exhale), light stretching of trained areas.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (Foundation)
Goals: Groove technique, improve insulin sensitivity with frequent large-muscle lifts, establish fueling rhythm, sleep regularity.

Week 1 (Jun 1–7)
- Lower A
  - Back squat or safety bar squat 3x6 @RPE7
  - Romanian deadlift 3x8 @RPE7
  - Split squat (rear foot elevated optional) 3x8/side @RPE8
  - Leg curl (seated/lying) 3x10 @RPE8
  - Standing calf raise 3x12 @RPE8
  - Pallof press 3x10/side
- Upper A
  - Bench press (barbell or DB) 4x6 @RPE7
  - One-arm DB row 3x8/side @RPE8
  - Seated cable row (neutral) 3x10 @RPE8
  - DB incline press 3x8 @RPE8
  - Cable face pull 3x12
  - Side plank 3x30–40s/side
- Lower B
  - Trap-bar deadlift 4x5 @RPE7
  - Front-foot elevated split squat 3x10/side
  - Hip thrust (barbell) 3x8 @RPE8
  - Leg press 2x12 @RPE8
  - Hanging knee raise 3x10
- Upper B
  - Overhead press 3x6 @RPE7
  - Lat pulldown (wide-neutral) 3x8 @RPE8
  - Chest-supported incline DB row 3x10
  - Cable fly or pec deck 2x12
  - DB lateral raise 3x12–15
  - Cable triceps pressdown 2x12, DB curls 2x12
- Optional LISS (Wed/Sat): 25–30 min brisk incline walk or bike, HR ~60–65% max; keep conversational.

Week 2
- Progress load 2–3% on main lifts if RPE <7.5 last week; add 1 set to hip thrust and rows.
- Swap one squat pattern if needed for comfort (e.g., high bar to SSB).
- Add anti-rotation carry: suitcase carry 2x30–40m/side on Lower B.

Week 3
- Keep exercises; try to add 1 rep per set on accessories or small load bump (1–2 kg).
- Upper: add 1 set to pulldown and lateral raise.
- Lower: pause RDL 2s just below knee on last set.

Week 4 (micro-deload-lite)
- Reduce sets by ~25%, keep intensity RPE 6–7.
- Focus on perfect reps, tempo control, and recovery.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (Hypertrophy with strength anchors)
Goals: Increase training volume modestly, maintain insulin-sensitizing stimulus via large compound lifts at moderate loads, add metabolic finishers sparingly.

Week 5
- Lower A
  - Back squat 4x5 @RPE7–8
  - RDL 4x6 @RPE7–8
  - Walking lunge 3x10/leg
  - Seated leg curl 3x10–12
  - Standing calf raise 4x10–12
  - Ab wheel or stability ball rollout 3x8–10
- Upper A
  - Bench press 4x5 @RPE7–8
  - One-arm DB row 4x8
  - Pull-up or assisted 3x6–8 (add band as needed)
  - DB incline press 3x8–10
  - Face pull 3x12–15
  - Side plank reach-through 3x8/side
- Lower B
  - Trap-bar deadlift 4x4–5 @RPE7–8
  - Hip thrust 4x6–8
  - Hack squat or leg press 3x10
  - Reverse hyper/back extension 3x12
  - Copenhagen side plank 2x20–30s/side
- Upper B
  - OHP 4x5 @RPE7–8
  - Chest-supported row 4x8–10
  - Lat pulldown 3x10
  - Cable fly 3x12
  - Lateral raise 3x12–15
  - Superset: cable curls 3x10–12 + rope pressdowns 3x10–12
- Optional finisher (choose 1–2 days max/week): 6–8 min sled push-drags or assault bike easy intervals (40s easy, 20s moderate x 8). Keep overall stress low.

Week 6
- Progress by load 2–3% or add 1 rep where possible within RPE targets.
- Add single-leg hinge: DB single-leg RDL 3x8/side on Lower B; remove reverse hyper if needed for time.
- Upper: add chest-supported Y-raise 2x12 for scap control.

Week 7
- Keep loads; add a set to main lower movement of each day (squat and trap-bar) if recovery is good.
- Introduce tempo on first accessory each day (e.g., 3s eccentric on DB incline and hip thrust, week only).

Week 8 (deload)
- Reduce sets by ~40–50%, keep RPE 6.
- Replace heavy pulls with technique work (e.g., trap-bar 3x3 @50–60% focusing on speed).
- Extra mobility and walking.

Phase 3: Weeks 9–11 (Intensification and metabolic density)
Goals: Slightly higher relative intensity, maintain total volume, increase density via shortened rest on accessories; keep CNS stress moderate. Continue to bias large muscle groups for glucose disposal.

Week 9
- Lower A
  - Back squat 5x3 @RPE7.5–8 (strength anchor)
  - RDL 3x6–7 @RPE8
  - Bulgarian split squat 3x10/side, 60–75s rest
  - Seated leg curl 3x12, 60s rest
  - Standing calf raise 3x12–15
  - Cable anti-rotation press 3x10/side
- Upper A
  - Bench press 5x3 @RPE7.5–8
  - Weighted or assisted pull-up 4x5–6
  - DB incline press 3x8, 60–75s rest
  - Chest-supported row 3x10, 60–75s rest
  - Face pull 3x15
  - Side plank 3x40–50s/side
- Lower B
  - Trap-bar deadlift 5x3 @RPE7.5–8
  - Hip thrust 3x6–8 @RPE8
  - Hack squat/leg press 3x10, 60–75s rest
  - Back extension 3x12
  - Hanging leg raise 3x10
- Upper B
  - OHP 5x3 @RPE7.5–8
  - Lat pulldown 3x8
  - Single-arm cable row 3x10/side, 60s rest
  - Cable fly 2x12–15
  - Lateral raise mechanical drop set x1 (partial reps after 10–12 full, keep form)
  - Arms: alt DB curl 2x12 + overhead rope extension 2x12
- Conditioning: Keep to 1–2 short LISS sessions; optional one 8–10 min EMOM sled/bike at easy-moderate.

Week 10
- Try +2–3% load on triples if previous week <8 RPE; otherwise hold and improve bar speed.
- Accessories: progress by 1 rep or small load; keep short rests on accessories.
- Add carries: farmer carry 3x30–40m on Lower A.

Week 11
- Strength anchors: 4x3 @RPE8–8.5 then 1 AMRAP technical set at RPE 9 cap on squat and bench only; stop 0–1 rep before true failure.
- Maintain density. If fatigue rises, remove one accessory per session.

Week 12 (Deload, testing, transition)
- Reduce to 2 full-body sessions + 1 easy LISS.
- Full-body A
  - Squat 3x3 @~70% recent best, bar speed focus
  - Bench 3x3 @~70%
  - RDL 2x6 light
  - Row 2x8
  - Core, mobility
- Full-body B
  - Trap-bar deadlift 3x3 @~70%
  - OHP 3x3 @~70%
  - Hip thrust 2x6 light
  - Pulldown 2x10
  - Core, mobility
- Optional testing at end of week: estimated 1RM via RPE single @8 for squat/bench/trap-bar; or rep PRs (e.g., 6–10RM) for less stress.
- Plan next block based on preferences and outcomes.

Recovery, stress management, and cycle considerations
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours/night, consistent schedule; morning light exposure; limit screens 60 min pre-bed.
- Stress: 5–10 min daily breathwork; walking after meals 10–15 min improves postprandial glucose.
- Menstrual irregularity: Expect variable energy. If signs of high fatigue, poor sleep, elevated resting HR, or heavier/longer bleed:
  - Drop one accessory per session and/or reduce top set RPE by 0.5–1 for 3–5 days.
  - Swap LISS days for mobility only.
- Soreness rule: If DOMS >48–72h or performance drops, hold loads and reduce sets next similar session.

Nutrition guidelines (anti-restriction, insulin sensitivity focus)
- Calorie target: gentle deficit or maintenance depending on stress/readiness.
  - Start at estimated maintenance (BW lb x 14–15 ≈ 1700–1850 kcal/day for 28 BMI typical; customize from food logs).
  - If energy, sleep, and cycle are stable after week 2, consider a modest deficit of 200–300 kcal/day; avoid >500 kcal deficits.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day (evenly across 3–4 meals). Example 110–140 g/day.
- Carbs: 2.5–4 g/kg/day depending on activity and tolerance; bias carbs around training:
  - Pre (60–120 min): 25–45 g low-fiber carbs + 20–30 g protein.
  - Post (0–2 h): 40–70 g carbs + 25–35 g protein.
  - Emphasize whole-food carbs with fiber at other meals; include resistant starches.
- Fats: 0.8–1.0 g/kg/day; include omega-3 sources 2–3x/week.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day from vegetables, legumes, oats, berries, chia/flax; supports satiety and glycemia.
- Meal timing: 3–4 consistent meals/day; avoid prolonged fasting given HPA sensitivity; last meal 2–3 h before bed with protein + complex carb to support sleep.
- Hydration/electrolytes: 30–35 ml/kg water/day; add sodium on training days if low BP or heavy sweat.
- Supplements (if approved by physician):
  - Myo-inositol 2 g + D-chiro-inositol 50–100 mg twice daily has evidence for PCOS insulin sensitivity and ovulatory function.
  - Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day.
  - Vitamin D3 if deficient; EPA/DHA 1–2 g/day via fish oil if dietary intake low.
  - Magnesium glycinate 200–400 mg at night for sleep/stress.
  - Caffeine modestly (≤3 mg/kg) pre-workout if well-tolerated; avoid late day.
- Alcohol: minimize; it can blunt recovery and worsen glycemia.

Progress targets and monitoring
- Strength: aim for +5–10% on 5RM/8RM patterns by week 11.
- Volume tolerance: total hard sets per muscle group around 10–14/week by Phase 2; adjust up/down by 2–4 sets based on recovery.
- Body composition: look for steady waist/hip reductions and improved gym performance rather than aggressive scale loss.
- Glycemia: if possible, track fasting glucose 1–2x/week; optional CGM for 2 weeks in phases 1 and 2 to assess meal responses.

Session notes and cues
- Focus on controlled eccentrics (2–3s), powerful concentric without grinding.
- Use bracing and neutral spine on squats/deadlifts; range of motion prioritized over load.
- Stop sets if technique degrades; quality over quantity to protect nervous system.

Contingencies for high-stress weeks
- Convert a full week to a low-stress template:
  - Two full-body sessions (A/B) of 6–8 total sets each @RPE 6–7.
  - Walks after meals, no finishers, extra sleep.
  - Resume plan next week.

This plan balances progressive resistance training with careful management of cardio and recovery to improve insulin sensitivity and body composition without provoking HPA dysfunction. Adjust loads by RPE, keep nutrition steady, and favor consistency over intensity spikes.
